title: Engram config/read borrows the rollout-replay timeout budget and doubles worst-case new-thread failure latency
outcome:
Claude review session-6531, Medium at src/codex_engram_bootstrap.rs:99.

The config/read wait reuses SHARED_CODEX_THREAD_SETUP_TIMEOUT (180s silence) and
SHARED_CODEX_RESPONSE_MAX_WAIT_WHILE_ACTIVE (900s active). Those budgets have a
documented rationale at src/codex.rs:924-954, and it is `thread/resume`
REPLAYING TENS TO HUNDREDS OF MEGABYTES OF ROLLOUT. A config/read is a cheap
local read and cannot justify that patience.

Because the read is now SEQUENTIAL with the thread/start wait, a first prompt on
a busy shared app-server can sit up to 900s in config/read and then up to 900s
in thread/start: ABOUT THIRTY MINUTES BEFORE THE USER SEES AN ERROR, where the
pre-change worst case was about fifteen.

FIX DIRECTION: give config/read its own, much tighter deadline constant instead
of borrowing the replay budget. The borrowed constant is also why a stale doc
comment now misdescribes its callers - see the related hygiene item.
